note: Shared by the Nightfall launcher and website. Regexes are JavaScript syntax, matched case-insensitively and multi-line.

entries.title: Out of memory (Java heap space)
entries.cause: The game used all the RAM it was given. Big modpacks, high render distance and shaders are the usual reasons.
fixes: Raise this instance’s memory by 2 GB (most modpacks want 4–8 GB).
Lower render distance and turn off shaders, then try again.
Remove or update memory-heavy mods; add FerriteCore and ModernFix if you use Fabric/Forge.
Close browsers and other games while playing.

entries.title: Out of memory (Metaspace)
entries.cause: Java ran out of space for class data, which happens with very large modpacks or a too-small MaxMetaspaceSize flag.
fixes: Remove any -XX:MaxMetaspaceSize flag from the extra JVM arguments.
Raise the instance memory by 2 GB.
Use the Java version Nightfall picks automatically.

entries.title: Out of direct buffer memory
entries.cause: Native (off-heap) memory ran out, usually from huge texture packs, shaders or a 32-bit Java.
fixes: Use a smaller resource pack or turn off shaders.
Make sure you use 64-bit Java (clear the custom Java path).
Raise memory by 2 GB.

entries.title: Unable to create native thread
entries.cause: The system refused to create more threads, often because the PC itself is out of memory or a mod leaks threads.
fixes: Close other programs and try again.
Lower the instance memory if it is more than half your PC’s RAM.
Update or remove the mod named in the stack trace.

entries.title: Could not reserve enough space for object heap
sig: Could not reserve enough space for (\d+KB )?object heap
entries.cause: Java could not get the RAM you set. Either the value is larger than your free memory, or a 32-bit Java is in use (max ~1.5 GB).
fixes: Lower the memory slider (keep at least 2 GB free for Windows).
Clear the custom Java path so Nightfall uses its own 64-bit Java.
Remove -Xmx/-Xms from the extra JVM arguments; the slider already sets them.

entries.title: Could not create the Java Virtual Machine
sig: Error: Could not create the Java Virtual Machine
Error occurred during initialization of VM
entries.cause: Java refused to start, nearly always because of a wrong flag in the extra JVM arguments or a memory value it cannot reserve.
fixes: Clear the extra JVM arguments.
Lower the memory slider.
Clear the custom Java path.

entries.title: GC overhead limit exceeded
entries.cause: Java spent almost all its time cleaning memory, a sign the game is about to run out of RAM.
fixes: Raise memory by 2 GB.
Lower render distance/simulation distance.
Remove heavy mods or resource packs.

entries.title: Too much RAM allocated (stutters / freezes)
entries.cause: Giving Minecraft nearly all your RAM starves Windows and causes stutters or crashes. More is not always better.
fixes: Set memory to about half of your PC’s RAM, and no more than 8–10 GB for most packs.
Use the recommended value on the memory slider.

entries.title: Java is too old (UnsupportedClassVersionError)
sig: has been compiled by a more recent version of the Java Runtime
entries.cause: The game or a mod needs a newer Java than the one used. Minecraft 1.17 needs Java 16+, 1.18–1.20.4 need Java 17, 1.20.5+ needs Java 21.
fixes: Clear the custom Java path so Nightfall downloads the correct Java automatically.
If you must use your own Java, install Java 21 (for 1.20.5+) or 17 (1.18–1.20.4).

entries.title: Java is too new for this version
sig: java\.lang\.ClassCastException: class jdk\.internal\.loader\.ClassLoaders\$AppClassLoader cannot be cast to class java\.net\.URLClassLoader
Unable to make field .* accessible: module java\.base does not "opens
entries.cause: Old Minecraft (1.16 and older) and old Forge need Java 8. Running them on Java 17/21 breaks the class loader.
fixes: Clear the custom Java path so Nightfall uses Java 8 for this version.
For Forge 1.12.2 and older, Java 8 is required.

entries.title: 32-bit Java in use
entries.cause: 32-bit Java can only use about 1.5 GB of RAM and is much slower.
fixes: Clear the custom Java path (Nightfall downloads 64-bit Java).
Uninstall old 32-bit Java from Windows.

entries.title: Java executable not found
entries.cause: The Java path in settings points to a file that does not exist (Java was uninstalled or moved).
fixes: Clear the custom Java path; Nightfall downloads Java automatically.
Or pick the java.exe inside your Java’s bin folder.

entries.title: Java runtime is broken or incomplete
sig: Error opening zip file or JAR manifest missing
Error: Could not find or load main class
entries.cause: The Java installation is incomplete (interrupted download, antivirus removed a file) or the classpath is broken.
fixes: Remove the Java runtime in Settings → Java; it re-downloads on next launch.
Repair the instance.
Add the Nightfall folder to your antivirus exclusions.

entries.title: Java module access error (add-opens)
entries.cause: An old mod uses Java internals that newer Java blocks.
fixes: Update the mod named in the error.
Use the Java version Nightfall picks for this Minecraft version.

entries.title: Fabric: mod requires another mod
sig: Mod resolution encountered an incompatible mod set
entries.cause: A Fabric/Quilt mod needs a library mod (often Fabric API, Cloth Config, Architectury) or a specific version of it.
fixes: Read the first "requires" line: it names the missing mod and version.
Install the missing mod from Browse (Fabric API is the most common).
Or disable the mod that needs it.
Use the Updates tab to bring all mods to matching versions.

entries.title: Fabric API is missing
entries.cause: Almost every Fabric mod needs Fabric API, and it is not installed.
fixes: Install Fabric API from Browse (Nightfall picks the version that matches).

entries.title: Fabric: incompatible mods
entries.cause: Two mods declare that they cannot run together (for example OptiFine/OptiFabric with Sodium).
fixes: Disable one of the two mods named in the log.
Use Sodium + Iris instead of OptiFine on Fabric.

entries.title: Mod is for a different Minecraft version
entries.cause: A mod was made for another Minecraft version.
fixes: Download the build of that mod for your exact Minecraft version (Browse filters this automatically).
Or remove the mod.

entries.title: Mod for the wrong loader
sig: is a Forge mod.*Fabric|is a Fabric mod.*Forge
Found a Forge mod in a Fabric|Found Fabric mod.*Forge
Mod file .* is (missing|not) a valid mod
is not a valid mod file
entries.cause: A Forge mod was dropped into a Fabric instance (or the other way round). Each loader only runs its own mods.
fixes: Remove the mod and download the version for your loader, or use Sinytra Connector on Forge/NeoForge if you know what you are doing.
Quilt can run most Fabric mods, but not Forge mods.

entries.title: Duplicate mods
entries.cause: The same mod is installed twice, usually an old and a new version side by side.
fixes: Open the Content tab and remove the older copy.
Check the mods folder for "(1).jar" style copies.

entries.title: Mixin apply failed
entries.cause: A mod tried to patch Minecraft code that changed or that another mod already patched. The log names the mod.
fixes: Look for "for mod <name>" in the error and update or disable that mod.
Update all mods (Updates tab).
If it started after adding a mod, disable that one first.

entries.title: Two mods patch the same code
entries.cause: Two mods change the same part of the game in incompatible ways.
fixes: Disable recently added mods one at a time to find the pair.
Check each mod page for known incompatibilities.

entries.title: Class not found / method missing
entries.cause: A mod was built against a different Minecraft, loader or library version, or a library mod is missing.
fixes: Check the class name in the error: it usually contains the mod’s package name.
Update that mod and its libraries, or remove it.
Make sure loader and Fabric API are up to date.

entries.title: Forge/NeoForge: missing or unsupported mods
entries.cause: Forge/NeoForge stopped because a mod is missing a dependency or the versions do not match.
fixes: Read the "Mod X requires Y" line and install Y in the version it asks for.
Make sure the Forge/NeoForge version is new enough for your mods.

entries.title: Forge: mods have errors (FML error screen)
entries.cause: One or more mods crashed while loading. The mod is named in "Caught exception from".
fixes: Find "Caught exception from <mod>" and update or remove that mod.
Check that the mod matches your Minecraft and Forge version.

entries.title: Forge mods in a NeoForge instance (or reverse)
entries.cause: NeoForge 1.20.2+ no longer loads Forge mods (and Forge does not load NeoForge mods).
fixes: Download the NeoForge version of the mod.
Or use a Forge instance for Forge-only mods.

entries.title: Quilt: mod loading failed
entries.cause: Quilt could not load a mod, usually a missing dependency or a Fabric mod that needs Fabric-only internals.
fixes: Install Quilted Fabric API (QFAPI) instead of plain Fabric API.
Update or remove the mod named in the error.

entries.title: Loader is too old for a mod
entries.cause: A mod needs a newer Fabric/Quilt/Forge loader than the one this instance uses.
fixes: Edit the instance and pick the newest loader version.

entries.title: Broken or corrupted mod file
entries.cause: A mod .jar is damaged (incomplete download, or it is not really a jar).
fixes: Remove the mod named in the log and reinstall it from Browse.
Never download mods from re-upload sites; use Modrinth or CurseForge.

entries.title: Corrupted mod config
entries.cause: A mod’s config file is broken (often after a crash or a manual edit).
fixes: Delete the config file named in the log from the instance’s config folder; the mod recreates it.

entries.title: OptiFine with Fabric/Sodium
entries.cause: OptiFine does not work well with modern mods. On Fabric it conflicts with Sodium/Iris and many others.
fixes: Remove OptiFine/OptiFabric and use Sodium + Iris (Recommendations → Performance) for the same benefits.

entries.title: OptiFine incompatible with Forge mods
entries.cause: OptiFine conflicts with Embeddium/Rubidium/Oculus and many Forge mods, and must match the exact Forge version.
fixes: Remove OptiFine and use Embeddium + Oculus instead.
If you keep it, use the OptiFine build that matches your Forge version exactly.

entries.title: Sodium/Iris version mismatch
entries.cause: Iris needs one specific Sodium version.
fixes: Update Sodium and Iris together from the Updates tab.

entries.title: Shader pack failed to compile
entries.cause: The shader pack does not support your GPU, driver or Iris version.
fixes: Turn shaders off (press O in game with Iris) or choose another pack.
Update your GPU driver.
Update Iris.

entries.title: Shaders ran out of GPU memory
entries.cause: Shaders plus high resolution packs needed more video memory than your GPU has.
fixes: Use a lighter shader profile or turn shaders off.
Lower render distance and resource pack resolution.

entries.title: Rendering mod conflict
entries.cause: Two rendering mods both try to replace the same renderer.
fixes: Keep only one renderer mod (Sodium on Fabric, Embeddium on Forge).

entries.title: Ticking entity crash
entries.cause: An entity (mob, item, minecart) in the world causes a crash every time it updates, usually from a mod bug.
fixes: Update the mod that adds the entity (see "Entity Type" in the report).
Back up the world, then remove the entity with a tool like MCA Selector or by setting "removeErroringEntities" in the mod’s config (Forge).
Restore an older backup of the world.

entries.title: Ticking block entity crash
entries.cause: A block entity (chest, machine, furnace) crashes when it updates.
fixes: Update the mod that adds the block (see "Block type" in the report).
On Forge, set removeErroringBlockEntities=true in config/forge-common.toml, play once, then turn it off.
Restore a world backup.

entries.title: Exception ticking world
entries.cause: Something in the world crashed the internal server (chunk, entity or a mod’s world logic).
fixes: Update all mods.
Try the world with recently added mods disabled.
Restore a backup from the Worlds tab.

entries.title: World or chunk is corrupted
sig: Chunk file at .* is in the wrong location
entries.cause: A world file was damaged (power loss, crash during save, or a disk issue).
fixes: Restore a backup from the Worlds tab.
Rename level.dat_old to level.dat inside the world folder.
Use MCA Selector to delete only the broken chunks.

entries.title: World saved in a newer version
entries.cause: Opening a world in an older Minecraft version than it was last played in can corrupt it.
fixes: Open the world in the same or a newer Minecraft version.
Back it up before switching versions.

entries.title: Missing blocks/items after removing mods
entries.cause: The world contains things from a mod that is no longer installed.
fixes: Reinstall the removed mod, or accept the warning knowing those blocks/items will be deleted.
Back up the world first.

entries.title: Data pack failed to load
entries.cause: A data pack (in the world or from a mod) has errors.
fixes: Start the world in Safe Mode from the error screen.
Remove the broken data pack from the world’s datapacks folder.
Update mods that add recipes or worldgen.

entries.title: World is open in another game (session.lock)
sig: The save is being accessed from another location
entries.cause: Another Minecraft window or a backup program is using the world.
fixes: Close other Minecraft windows and backup/sync tools (OneDrive) and try again.
Move the instance out of OneDrive-synced folders.

entries.title: Pixel format not accelerated
sig: WGL: The driver does not appear to support OpenGL
entries.cause: Windows is using a basic display driver, or the game runs on a GPU without OpenGL support.
fixes: Install the latest driver from your GPU maker (NVIDIA, AMD or Intel), not just Windows Update.
On laptops, set Java (javaw.exe) to use the dedicated GPU in Windows Graphics settings.
Remote Desktop sessions do not support OpenGL; play locally.

entries.title: OpenGL version not supported (GLFW 65543)
sig: WGL: OpenGL profile requested but WGL_ARB_create_context_profile is unavailable
entries.cause: Minecraft 1.17+ needs OpenGL 3.2. The GPU or its driver is too old.
fixes: Update the GPU driver.
Very old Intel HD (2nd/3rd gen) GPUs cannot run 1.17+; play 1.16.5 or older.

entries.title: GLFW error 65544 / window could not be created
sig: Failed to create the GLFW window
entries.cause: The game could not open a window, usually a graphics driver or display configuration problem.
fixes: Update the GPU driver.
Disconnect extra monitors and try again.
Turn off "Start in fullscreen" for this instance.

entries.title: Intel graphics driver crash
entries.cause: A known crash in Intel’s OpenGL driver.
fixes: Install the newest Intel graphics driver from intel.com (not the laptop maker’s old one).
On laptops with NVIDIA/AMD, make Java use that GPU instead.

entries.title: AMD graphics driver crash
entries.cause: A crash inside AMD’s OpenGL driver. Some driver versions have OpenGL bugs.
fixes: Update the AMD Adrenalin driver, or roll back one version if it started after an update.
Disable AMD overlays (Radeon overlay, Anti-Lag).

entries.title: NVIDIA graphics driver crash
entries.cause: A crash inside NVIDIA’s OpenGL driver, often fixed by a clean driver install.
fixes: Update the NVIDIA driver (choose "Clean installation").
Turn off "Threaded optimization" for javaw.exe in NVIDIA Control Panel if it persists.

entries.title: Native crash (EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION)
sig: A fatal error has been detected by the Java Runtime Environment
entries.cause: Java crashed in native code: usually a GPU driver, an overlay hooking the game, or a broken native library.
fixes: Update the GPU driver.
Turn off overlays: Discord, Steam, GeForce Experience, MSI Afterburner/RivaTuner, OBS game capture.
Look at the "Problematic frame" line: a .dll name there points to the culprit.

entries.title: Overlay or recording software crash
entries.cause: An overlay (RivaTuner, Discord, OBS, Steam, Overwolf) injected into the game and crashed it.
fixes: Disable the overlay for Minecraft/javaw.exe or close that program.
Update the overlay software.

entries.title: OpenGL Error 1282
entries.cause: A rendering mod or shader issued an invalid OpenGL call. Usually harmless spam, sometimes black screens.
fixes: Turn shaders off to test.
Update Sodium/Iris/OptiFine.
Disable "Show GL errors" in video settings if it is just spam.

entries.title: Black or white screen on start
entries.cause: The game could not create its drawing surfaces, usually a driver issue or a resource pack with huge textures.
fixes: Update the GPU driver.
Remove large resource packs.
Turn off fullscreen and set a normal window size.

entries.title: Texture atlas too large
entries.cause: Too many or too large textures for your GPU’s maximum texture size (common with big modpacks + HD packs).
fixes: Remove HD resource packs.
Lower mipmap levels in video settings.
Raise memory if it is also low.

entries.title: LWJGL native library failed to load
sig: Can\'?t load (IA )?32-bit \.dll on a AMD 64-bit platform
entries.cause: The game’s native libraries are missing, blocked, or for the wrong architecture.
fixes: Repair the instance so natives are re-extracted.
Add the Nightfall folder to antivirus exclusions.
Clear the custom Java path (wrong 32/64-bit Java).

entries.title: Missing Visual C++ runtime
entries.cause: Windows is missing the Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable needed by some natives.
fixes: Install the latest "Visual C++ Redistributable x64" from Microsoft.

entries.title: Sound engine failed (OpenAL)
entries.cause: No audio device, or another app has exclusive control of it. The game keeps running without sound.
fixes: Plug in or enable an audio device and restart the game.
Turn off "exclusive mode" for your audio device in Windows Sound settings.

entries.title: Exit code 1
entries.cause: A generic Java error. The real reason is earlier in the log or crash report.
fixes: Open the latest log and look for the first "Exception" or "Error" line.
Check the other matches on this page for that line.
Disable recently added mods.

entries.title: Exit code -1
entries.cause: The game stopped abruptly, usually a mod crash before logging finished or a driver problem.
fixes: Check the crash report; if none, update GPU drivers.
Disable recently added mods.
Repair the instance.

entries.title: Exit code -805306369
entries.cause: Windows ended Java (0xCFFFFFFF). Commonly memory exhaustion, an incompatible mod, or GPU driver trouble.
fixes: Raise memory by 2 GB, but keep half your RAM free.
Update GPU drivers.
Disable recently added mods or shaders.

entries.title: Exit code -1073740791 / 1073740791 (0xC0000409)
entries.cause: A native "stack buffer overrun" crash. Almost always a GPU driver, overlay or a native mod library.
fixes: Update the GPU driver (clean install).
Close overlays (Discord, RivaTuner, OBS, Overwolf).
Remove mods that ship native code (e.g. voice chat, replay).

entries.title: Exit code -1073741819 (0xC0000005)
entries.cause: Access violation in native code: drivers, overlays, or antivirus injecting into Java.
fixes: Update GPU drivers.
Disable overlays and test with antivirus exclusions for the Nightfall folder.

entries.title: Exit code -1073741571 (stack overflow)
entries.cause: Infinite recursion, usually a mod bug or two mods calling each other.
fixes: Disable recently added mods.
Add -Xss4M to the extra JVM arguments only if a mod page tells you to.

entries.title: Exit code -1073741515 (missing DLL)
entries.cause: A required Windows DLL is missing, usually the Visual C++ runtime.
fixes: Install the latest Visual C++ Redistributable x64.
Clear the custom Java path.

entries.title: Exit code -1073741502 (DLL init failed)
entries.cause: A DLL failed to start, often antivirus or a broken system library.
fixes: Restart the PC.
Add the Nightfall folder to antivirus exclusions.
Install Visual C++ Redistributable x64.

entries.title: Exit code 137 (killed, out of memory)
entries.cause: The operating system killed the game because the computer ran out of memory.
fixes: Lower the instance memory so the PC has room.
Close other programs.

entries.title: Exit code 143 / killed
entries.cause: Something stopped the game from outside (task manager, Stop button, or the system).
fixes: If you did not stop it, check antivirus history for a blocked Java.

entries.title: Exit code 134 (abort)
entries.cause: Java aborted, often from a native library or driver assertion.
fixes: Update GPU drivers.
Repair the instance.

entries.title: Exit code 255
entries.cause: A general failure that happens before Minecraft starts, often Java or classpath trouble.
fixes: Clear the custom Java path and extra JVM arguments.
Repair the instance.

entries.title: Game closed right after starting (exit 0)
entries.cause: The game exited normally very quickly: usually Forge/Fabric showed an error screen and you closed it, or the window failed silently.
fixes: Open the latest log to see the last lines.
Check mods for missing dependencies.

entries.title: Download corrupted (hash mismatch)
entries.cause: A file arrived damaged or was changed by a proxy/antivirus.
fixes: Repair the instance (it re-downloads broken files).
Try again later or on another network.

entries.title: Download failed / no internet
entries.cause: A server could not be reached: no internet, DNS trouble, or a firewall/VPN blocking it.
fixes: Check your internet connection and try again.
Turn off VPN/proxy, or allow Nightfall in your firewall.
Lower parallel downloads in Settings on slow connections.

entries.title: SSL / certificate error
sig: unable to (find valid|get local issuer) certification
entries.cause: Secure connections are being intercepted (antivirus HTTPS scanning, school/work proxy) or the PC clock is wrong.
fixes: Set the Windows clock to update automatically.
Turn off HTTPS scanning in your antivirus, or try another network.

entries.title: Missing assets (no sounds, purple-black textures)
entries.cause: Game assets were not fully downloaded.
fixes: Repair the instance.

entries.title: Missing library / classpath error
sig: Could not find or load main class (net\.minecraft|cpw|net\.fabricmc|org\.quiltmc|net\.neoforged)
Error: Unable to initialize main class
entries.cause: A library jar is missing or damaged, so Java cannot find the game.
fixes: Repair the instance.
Add the Nightfall folder to antivirus exclusions.

entries.title: Antivirus or firewall blocked the game
sig: The process cannot access the file because it is being used
Operation did not complete successfully because the file contains a virus
entries.cause: Security software locked, quarantined or blocked a game file or Java.
fixes: Add the Nightfall data folder and javaw.exe to your antivirus exclusions.
Restore quarantined files, then repair the instance.
Allow javaw.exe in Windows Firewall for multiplayer.

entries.title: Folder path with special characters
entries.cause: The game folder path contains characters some mods cannot handle (non-Latin letters, !, # or very long paths).
fixes: Move the Nightfall data folder to a simple path like C:\Nightfall (Settings → Data folder).
Avoid "!" and "#" in folder names.

entries.title: Instance inside OneDrive / cloud folder
entries.cause: Cloud sync locks files while the game writes them, causing failed saves and crashes.
fixes: Keep the Nightfall data folder outside OneDrive/Dropbox/Google Drive.

entries.title: Disk is full
sig: There is not enough space on the disk
entries.cause: The drive ran out of space while downloading or saving.
fixes: Free some disk space (Java + assets need about 1–2 GB per version).
Delete old instances or backups you do not need.

entries.title: File in use by another program
entries.cause: Another program (a second game window, backup tool, antivirus scan) has the file open.
fixes: Close other Minecraft windows and try again.
Restart the PC if it persists.

entries.title: Permission denied
entries.cause: Nightfall or Java cannot write to the folder.
fixes: Do not run the game from Program Files; keep the data folder in your user folder.
Check that the folder is not read-only.

entries.title: Forge installer: launcher_profiles.json
sig: There is no minecraft launcher profile
entries.cause: The Forge installer expected the official launcher’s files.
fixes: Nightfall creates this file itself; repair the instance and try again.

entries.title: Forge/NeoForge installer failed
entries.cause: The loader installer could not finish, usually a download problem or a too-old Java for the installer.
fixes: Try again (downloads sometimes fail).
Choose a different (newer) loader version in Edit instance.
Fabric/Quilt are more reliable if your mods support them.

entries.title: Version file damaged
entries.cause: A downloaded version/profile file is incomplete.
fixes: Repair the instance.

entries.title: No Xbox profile (XSTS 2148916233)
entries.cause: The Microsoft account has never signed in to Xbox, so it has no Xbox profile.
fixes: Sign in once at xbox.com (or minecraft.net) to create the profile, then sign in to Nightfall again.

entries.title: Xbox not available in your country (2148916235)
entries.cause: Xbox Live is not available in the account’s country/region.
fixes: The account region cannot be changed easily; contact Xbox support.

entries.title: Adult verification needed (2148916236 / 2148916237)
entries.cause: South Korean accounts must complete age verification on xbox.com.
fixes: Sign in at xbox.com and complete adult verification, then try again.

entries.title: Child account needs family approval (2148916238)
entries.cause: The account is under 18 and must be added to a Microsoft Family group by an adult.
fixes: Ask a parent to add the account at account.microsoft.com/family and allow Xbox/Minecraft.

entries.title: Xbox account banned or suspended
entries.cause: The Xbox account is banned or suspended.
fixes: Check enforcement.xbox.com for details.

entries.title: Xbox terms need accepting (2148916234)
entries.cause: The account must accept the latest Xbox terms of use.
fixes: Sign in at xbox.com and accept the terms, then sign in to Nightfall again.

entries.title: Parental controls block online play (2148916229)
entries.cause: Family settings do not allow this account to play online/multiplayer.
fixes: A parent can allow multiplayer in the Xbox Family Settings app.

entries.title: Account does not own Minecraft: Java Edition
entries.cause: The signed-in Microsoft account has no Java Edition licence or no player name yet.
fixes: Use the account that bought Minecraft (Game Pass PC also counts).
Create your player name once at minecraft.net/profile.

entries.title: Waiting for Mojang approval (403)
entries.cause: Microsoft and Xbox sign-in worked, but Mojang has not approved this launcher’s app ID yet.
fixes: Nothing is wrong with your account. Use dev mode for offline singleplayer testing until approval.

entries.title: Sign-in expired
entries.cause: The saved sign-in is no longer valid (password changed, signed out everywhere, or 90 days unused).
fixes: Remove the account and sign in again.

entries.title: Sign-in code expired
entries.cause: The Microsoft code was not entered in time, or the request was declined.
fixes: Start sign-in again and enter the new code within 15 minutes.

entries.title: Too many requests (429)
entries.cause: Mojang or Microsoft temporarily limited requests from your network.
fixes: Wait a few minutes and try again.

entries.title: Invalid session when joining a server
sig: Failed to log in: Invalid session
entries.cause: The server could not verify your login with Mojang: an expired token, or an offline/dev profile on an online-mode server.
fixes: Restart Nightfall so the token refreshes, then join again.
Dev mode profiles cannot join online-mode servers.

entries.title: Outdated client / server
entries.cause: Your Minecraft version differs from the server’s.
fixes: Create or switch to an instance with the server’s version (shown in the server list ping).
Some servers allow newer clients through ViaVersion, not older ones.

entries.title: Connection refused
entries.cause: Nothing is listening at that address/port: the server is offline, the address is wrong, or a firewall blocks it.
fixes: Check the server address and port.
Check if the server is online (server list ping).
Allow javaw.exe through Windows Firewall.

entries.title: Connection timed out
entries.cause: The server did not answer in time: it is down, far away, or a firewall/VPN drops the traffic.
fixes: Try again; check the server status.
Turn off VPN, or try another network.

entries.title: Unknown host
entries.cause: The server address could not be found (typo or DNS issue).
fixes: Check the spelling of the server address.
Try a public DNS like 1.1.1.1.

entries.title: Mod mismatch with server
sig: This server has mods that require
entries.cause: The server and your instance have different mods or mod versions.
fixes: Use the server’s modpack (import its .mrpack) so versions match exactly.

entries.title: Chat signing / profile key error
sig: Invalid signature for profile public key
entries.cause: The server requires signed chat but the profile key is missing or expired.
fixes: Restart Nightfall and the game so a new key is fetched.
Dev mode/offline profiles cannot use signed chat.

entries.title: Banned or not whitelisted
entries.cause: The server does not allow your account.
fixes: Contact the server staff.

entries.title: Multiplayer is disabled
entries.cause: Account or family settings block multiplayer.
fixes: A parent can allow multiplayer in Xbox Family Settings.
Check xbox.com privacy settings: "You can join multiplayer games" must be allowed.

entries.title: Server is full
entries.cause: The server reached its player limit.
fixes: Try again later.

entries.title: Game already running
entries.cause: This instance is already open.
fixes: Switch to the open game window, or press Stop in Nightfall.

entries.title: Generic mod crash (crash report names a mod)
entries.cause: The crash report lists the mod it suspects.
fixes: Update the suspected mod, or disable it to confirm.
Report the crash to that mod’s issue tracker with the mclo.gs link.

entries.title: Rendering overlay / screen crash
entries.cause: A menu or overlay crashed while drawing, usually a UI or HUD mod.
fixes: Update or disable HUD/menu mods (minimaps, mod menus, custom main menus).

entries.title: Keybind / controls crash
entries.cause: A mod registered a broken keybind.
fixes: Delete options.txt in the instance folder to reset controls (back it up first).

entries.title: Resource pack failed to load
entries.cause: A resource pack is broken or for another version.
fixes: Remove the pack from resourcepacks and restart.

entries.title: Wrong architecture natives (Apple/ARM)
entries.cause: Natives for the wrong CPU architecture were loaded.
fixes: Clear the custom Java path so a native Java is used.
Repair the instance.

entries.title: Nightfall companion mod problem
entries.cause: The small companion mod (in-game mod toggles) failed.
fixes: Update Nightfall; the companion mod is re-installed on launch.
You can disable it in the Content tab; the game works without it.
